merger_description:
Blackbird HP Pty Ltd, Blackbird Southern Land Pty Ltd, Blackbird Guardians Coinvestment Pty Ltd, Blackbird Purple Pty Ltd, Blackbird Hotham Pty Ltd, Blackbird CB Pty Limited, Blackbird FSA Pty Ltd and Blackbird Aware Pty Limited (the **Blackbird Funds**) propose to purchase shares of Series F Preferred Stock in a capital raise by Baseten Labs, Inc (**Baseten**).

The Blackbird Funds are venture capital co-investment fund vehicles managed by Blackbird Ventures Pty Ltd (**Blackbird Ventures**). Blackbird Ventures is a venture capital firm based in Australia and New Zealand that invests in early-stage and high-growth technology companies. Funds managed by Blackbird Ventures (including the Blackbird Funds) hold minority investments in hundreds of companies in Australia, New Zealand, the United States of America and around the world.

Baseten is a provider of an artificial intelligence (**AI**) inference platform and is based in San Francisco. Baseten's platform enables customers to deploy AI models across multiple clouds, regions, and geographies through its multi-tenant, single-tenant, and self-hosted deployment options. Baseten also offers advanced on-demand AI training capabilities for companies deploying custom or fine-tuned models. The Baseten platform encompasses models across various modality and use cases, including large language models, speech-to-text, text-to-speech, image generation, video generation, embeddings, and multi-model workflows.

determination_table_content.details:
Blackbird HP Pty Ltd, Blackbird Southern Land Pty Ltd, Blackbird
Guardians Coinvestment Pty Ltd, Blackbird Purple Pty Ltd, Blackbird
Hotham Pty Ltd, Blackbird CB Pty Limited, Blackbird FSA Pty Ltd and
Blackbird Aware Pty Limited (the Blackbird Funds) applied for a
notification waiver in respect of the Blackbird Funds’ proposed
acquisition of shares of Series F Preferred Stock in Baseten Labs,
Inc. (Baseten), as described in the transaction documents provided
as part of the application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The Blackbird Funds are venture capital co-investment fund vehicles
managed by Blackbird Ventures Pty Ltd (Blackbird Ventures).
Blackbird Ventures is a venture capital firm based in Australia and
New Zealand that invests in early-stage and high-growth technology
companies. Funds managed by Blackbird Ventures (including the
Blackbird Funds) hold minority investments in hundreds of
companies in Australia, New Zealand, the United States of America
and around the world.
The target, Baseten, is a provider of an artificial intelligence (AI)
inference platform and is based in San Francisco. Baseten's platform
enables customers to deploy AI models across multiple clouds,
regions, and geographies through its multi-tenant, single-tenant, and
self-hosted deployment options. Baseten also offers on demand AI
training capabilities for companies deploying custom or fine-tuned
models. The Baseten platform encompasses models across various
modality and use cases, including large language models, speech-to-
text, text-to-speech, image generation, video generation,
embeddings, and multi-model workflows.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided by the applicant, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition. In particular:
a. the size of the interest in Baseten being acquired by the
Blackbird Funds is small
b. there does not appear to be horizontal overlap between the
Blackbird Funds and Baseten, or between Blackbird
Ventures’ portfolio companies and Baseten, in the supply of
AI inference products in Australia
c. Baseten has a single customer in Australia
d. there appears to be a low risk of foreclosure or other
concerning vertical or conglomerate effects resulting from
exclusionary conduct, bundling or tying of products or
services post-acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
